I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. That is what fits my place best. Our county is on the North China Plain, the land and machinery are suited to wheat-maize double cropping, and at my age I want a system I know well, can manage on time, and can sell easily. I will not spread myself across many crops, because that raises labor, management mistakes, and market risk. I will use better seed, but I will not chase extreme input use. I care about steady yield, lower waste, and getting through the season with work I can actually handle. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease when needed. After wheat harvest, I will seed maize quickly, keep the stubble and use no-tillage to save time and moisture, then give one main topdressing and limited irrigation because summer rain does part of the work here.
